question: If \(\log_{10}m=b-\log_{10}n,\) then \(m=\)
solution:
The real logarithms require \(m>0\) and \(n>0\). Add \(\log_{10}n\) to both sides so that the product rule can combine the two logarithms:
\[
\log_{10}(mn)=\log_{10}m+\log_{10}n=b.
\]
By the definition of a base-10 logarithm, this means \(mn=10^b\). Because \(n>0\), division by \(n\) is valid, giving
\[
m=\frac{10^b}{n}.
\]
This is choice \(\mathrm{E}\).
